title: The Grandparent Phone Scam: Red Flags and How to Protect Family
bigPicture: A scammer pretends to be a grandchild in trouble and asks for money, hoping Grandma will send it quickly.
whatYouNeedToKnow: A scammer may call and say they need money for a car crash or jail fee.
They often ask you to keep the call secret and not tell anyone.
They may ask for gift cards or cash, which cannot be returned.
commonMistakesToAvoid: Sending money right away without checking.
Hanging up if you think it's a scam, instead of asking questions.
actionSteps: Ask the caller to call back later and let you check with another family member.
Call a trusted family member or the police to verify before sending any money.
